subject: Navitas preservation timebox proposal & SIG artifact request
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@navitashealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example
Cc: sec@navitashealth.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary extended retention for tenant debug traces

Hi Vanessa,

Quick one from our security team — we're preparing for a regulatory audit focused on incident forensics and need to confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a customer-specific timebox to preserve ephemeral inference traces (session debug data and selective KV cache snapshots) for 90 days rather than the default 30-day ephemeral retention.

Key asks:
- Can Redwood provide a tenant-scoped preservation window of 90 days for Navitas Health?
- What SIG/CAIQ/SOC2 evidence can you share that maps to controls around restricted access, tamper-evident storage, and export/audit logs for preserved traces?
- Any impact on cost/throughput we should expect (rough estimate ok).

I've attached a short RFP form with our scope (navitas_request_form.pdf). Sec team would like the evidence pack before EOD Friday so they can sign off on the exception.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Amy Chen
Security Lead, Navitas Health
amy.chen@navitashealth.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@navitashealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extended retention for tenant debug traces

Hi Amy — thanks for the clear scope and the attached form.

Short answers up front:
- We can support a customer-specific 90-day timebox for preserved ephemeral traces on a per-tenant basis; this typically requires an agreed preservation policy and a short operational runbook.
- We will assemble a SIG/CAIQ mapping and a SOC2-aligned evidence packet that highlights restricted access, immutable/auditable export paths, and the preservation lifecycle for the traces.
- Cost impact: expect a modest uplift driven by storage and longer-lived snapshot exports; I'll surface a rough estimate after confirming the expected ingested token volume and snapshot cadence.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben (cc'd) will outline the security artifacts and an initial evidence bundle we can share.
2) Karthik (cc'd) will confirm operational steps (where the preserved snapshots live, export cadence, sample export proofs).
3) I'll coordinate a short deliverable (evidence pack + timeline) by EOB Thursday so your team has it before Friday.

Ben/Karthik — can you confirm feasibility and if any legal sign-off is needed for the 90-day carveout?

Cheers,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@navitashealth.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extended retention for tenant debug traces

Amy / Vanessa —

We can pull together the artifacts Navitas needs. Summary of the plan from the security/controls side:

- Preservation model: Create a tenant-scoped 'kept-window' configuration (90 days) on the customer's Dedicated pool. Preserved data will be written to an immutable object store partition with versioned keys and server-side encryption (KMS).
- Access controls: Only a narrow RBAC role (Security:ReadExport) will be granted for exports; exports require an audited export job with signed requests and justification metadata.
- Tamper evidence & audit: Every export/store operation generates an append-only audit entry (WAL) stored in our audit cluster; we'll include hashed manifests for each snapshot in the evidence pack.
- Proof artifacts we'll provide: CAIQ mappings for the above controls, a SOC2-aligned narrative, sample audit log lines, a sample export manifest (signed), and a short runbook for initiating an evidence export.
- Cost note: Roughly +12–20% on storage/egress for the preserved windows depending on snapshot frequency. I'll work with Vanessa on exact numbers after we get your snapshot cadence.

I've staged an initial evidence folder here for Navitas (internal link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-navitas-evidence
We'll attach a zipped bundle for your team when ready.

Karthik — anything to add on the operational side?

Ben Carter
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@navitashealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.example, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extended retention for tenant debug traces

Amy — quick operational confirmation:

- We can enable the 90-day kept-window as a per-tenant flag; enabling will trigger a scheduled daily snapshot with incremental manifests retained for the configured window.
- Snapshots will be stored in a locked bucket with SSE-KMS and object versioning. We can provide a sample signed export manifest and S3 read-only temporary credentials for your security team to validate the export flow.
- Estimated timeline: enablement + evidence bundle delivery = 48 business hours after sign-off. We'll provide the zipped evidence pack (redwood_navitas_evidence_pack.zip) containing:
   * SIG-to-control mapping (CSV)
   * Sample audit logs (anonymized)
   * Export manifest + signature
   * Short runbook for Navitas security to request an export

Next step from our side: Vanessa will send the formal DocuSign engagement for the preservation addendum. Amy — if you can confirm scope in the attached RFP (we received navitas_request_form.pdf), we'll route the DocuSign and enable the kept-window upon signed agreement.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
